first.rationale: I intend to test shortening onboarding and reducing required signup fields because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, while prior evidence indicates these changes improved completion, time-to-value, and first-week activation. I will verify both archived records before committing and avoid promotional pricing because its acquisition lift came with materially worse 30-day retention. A standard experiment should provide meaningful evidence while limiting exposure.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded experiment shortening onboarding, prioritizing the directly relevant completion and activation declines. The verified result showed a durable +13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. Signup-field reduction is also supported for SMBs, but its -1% retention impact and lack of replication outside SMBs warrant treating it as a segment-specific follow-up rather than broadening it now. Monitor qualified revenue and 30-day retention as decision guardrails.

final2.rationale: Run a narrowly targeted, time-limited pricing test for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB accounts facing immediate competitive churn. Prior evidence shows acquisition and revenue lift but materially worse 30-day retention, so this should not become a broad rollout. Set strict guardrails on qualified revenue, gross margin, conversion, and 30-day retention, while preserving the onboarding experiment as the more sustainable baseline response.
